title: Испорченный соус и подозрительный постоялец  (The Ruined Sauce and the Suspicious Guest)

segments.t: In payback for the fire alarm, Mikhail ruins Barinov's thirty-eight-hour demi-glace sauce, and Vika breaks up their fight by claiming a fussy guest in glasses at reception is the secret inspector. Listen to the confrontation.
Ты чем думал, когда пожар в номере устроил?
Он стоит с чемоданом в очках.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Ты чем думал, когда пожар в номере устроил?
'What were you thinking when you started a fire in the room?' Mikhail addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to arrange'.
'Back off, I need to take the sauce off the heat.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to leave' before landing on 'need'.
'What have you just done?!' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'you', while 'make' completes the thought. Vika answers right away.
'Mikhail, it seems the secret guest has arrived.' The meaning hinges on 'Mikhail' working together with 'came' in spoken Russian.
'Which one? Where is he right now?' In Russian, the idea of 'who' flows naturally into 'now' without extra filler words.
'He is right here, next to the owner.' The meaning hinges on 'he' working together with 'with the owner' in spoken Russian. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Well, where is he standing over there?' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'come on', while 'is standing' completes the thought.
'There he is standing by the counter.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'over there' and finishing on 'counter'.
'Vitya, look, they are asking for you already.' Notice how Russian expresses 'proper name' and 'are asking for' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Он стоит с чемоданом в очках.
'He is standing with a suitcase in glasses.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'he' before landing on 'in glasses'.
'He is clearly dissatisfied with something already.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'he' and 'already' in a few short words.

'I will go prepare a welcome gift for him.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'will go', while 'gift' completes the thought. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Ты чем думал, когда пожар в номере устроил?
Он стоит с чемоданом в очках.
And that sets Vika's clever distraction in motion. Notice how 'with a suitcase in glasses' uses the instrumental case for the suitcase and prepositional for the glasses. See you in the next scene.
Только так можно остановить их войну.
